upstream.scope: Generic macOS client: the first bounded slice of D2 T38, a minimal Connect form (host, remote user, optional port, optional name) in client-owned chrome, over the existing SSHTransport, OpenSSH known_hosts and credential handling (§19, §19.1, §22.1, §25); endpoint validation before argv, strict non-interactive host-key policy with understandable blocking diagnostics, one launcher path for counter and srtop; no server, SDK, protocol, registry, proto, framing, generated-file or srtop change

entries.feature: ConnectionEndpoint.parse(host:user:port:): the Connect form's fields become a validated SSH destination; the Host field also takes user@host, host:port, [v6] and user@[v6]:port, and a user or port named twice must agree; hosts are ASCII names/IPv4 ([A-Za-z0-9._-], not starting with - or .) or inet_pton IPv6 literals in brackets with an optional %zone, at most 253 characters; users are [A-Za-z0-9._-], not starting with - or ., at most 64; ports are one to five ASCII digits naming 1-65535; names at most 128; bare IPv6, URLs, whitespace inside a value, shell metacharacters and non-ASCII are rejected with a specific message; ConnectDraft.validationMessage/savedConnection use it and an empty name defaults to the endpoint; round 2: before any per-field rule every field (host, user, port, name) and every saved host/user refuses NUL and any control, format, separator, surrogate, private-use or unassigned scalar (ParseError.controlCharacter); trimming drops only Zs spaces, tab, LF and CR; validateIPv6 refuses a literal with a NUL and calls inet_pton only when strlen equals the UTF-8 length, so it never passes on a prefix; round 3: every bound counts Unicode scalars (host field 326, host 253, user 64, port 5, name 128) and any field over 4096 UTF-8 bytes is refused before it is trimmed or scanned; every ParseError description echoes at most 32 scalars of input then '…'

ConnectionManager.sshConfiguration(for:) is the one SSH configuration every connection uses whatever app serves the srui subsystem (StrictHostKeyChecking=yes, BatchMode=yes, user's own agent/keys/known_hosts, fixed subsystem, -- before the host); connect(id:) re-validates a saved entry before it can become argv, so a tampered saved-connections file never reaches ssh; counter and srtop both connect through connect(_:) over a real localhost sshd and the real srui-ssh-bridge; round 2: validate(savedHost:user:port:) also refuses saved port 0 (65536 cannot be decoded and the file fails to load); pre-PX-023 entries the form would no longer produce are refused with 'Remove it and add it again'
entries.scope: PX-023/client-macos ConnectionManager/ConnectionManager.swift sshConfiguration(for:), connect(id:), beginAttempt; SRUITests ConnectionEndpointTests, ConnectionLauncherLiveTests

entries.feature: HostKeyRejection classifies OpenSSH's own unknown, changed, revoked and generic host-key failures, and only ssh's own: SSHTransport.localFailureBeforeStream() reports the child's stderr when it exited 255 before any stdout (SRUI stream) byte, LocalHostKeyRejection.diagnose turns it into ConnectionAttemptEvent.hostKeyRejected or a thrown LocalHostKeyRejection, and no failure string (which can carry server-authored SERVER HANDSHAKE_REFUSED detail) is ever classified; ConnectionManager presents it as a blocking ConnectionAlert.Kind.hostKeyRejected ('Host Key Not Trusted') naming the endpoint and known_hosts entry, saying SRUI never adds or replaces a key and how to verify it outside SRUI, followed by ssh's stderr; the alert's only action is OK; every other failure, including a server refusal that imitates host-key text, keeps Connection Failed; an unknown or changed key never runs the subsystem and leaves known_hosts byte-for-byte unchanged; round 3: every SSHConfiguration passes -o LogLevel=ERROR (LogLevel is a blocked extra option), so a server's pre-authentication Banner never reaches ssh's stderr, and HostKeyRejection is structural: the verdict must be ssh's last stderr line exactly 'Host key verification failed.', with the kind read from the line just before it, so a server disconnect reason or banner text before ssh's own last line never classifies

entries.feature: ConnectSheet: the Connect form as client chrome with Host, Remote User, optional Port and optional Name fields, the validation reason shown inline, Connect disabled and its action guarded until the endpoint is valid, Cancel and Connect as the sheet's cancel and default actions; a native AppKit test types into its NSTextFields and submits with Return; NUL in the host, user and port typed into the native fields never submits
